title: Quicksand server configuration
description: config.json for the Quicksand server. Add "$schema": "./config.schema.json" to a config file for autocompletion and checking in editors such as VS Code.

$schema.description: The schema this file follows, for editors.

listen.description: Address the HTTP server binds to.

database.description: Path of the SQLite database file.

secureCookies.description: Mark session cookies Secure. Enable when Quicksand is served over HTTPS (directly or behind a proxy).

tls.description: Serve HTTPS with this certificate. Browsers only allow clipboard access and audio decoding on secure origins, so serve over HTTPS (here or via a reverse proxy) anywhere but localhost.

cert.description: PEM certificate file path; may include intermediates.

pve.description: The Proxmox VE API Quicksand manages VMs through (see docs/proxmox-setup.md).

url.description: Base URL of the Proxmox API.

fingerprint.description: Pins the SHA-256 fingerprint of the API certificate (hex, colons optional). Leave empty to use the system trust store.

pool.description: Resource pool deployed VMs are created in. Grant the API token its VM privileges on /pool/<pool>. Required to deploy templates.

vmids.description: The range of Proxmox VM IDs deployments are created with. Required to deploy templates.

networks.description: Networks users can deploy onto. At least one is required to deploy templates.

agent.description: The optional in-guest agent. Required when any template has agent set (see docs/agent.md).

privateKey.description: Key Quicksand authenticates to agents with (create one with "quicksand agent keygen"). Agents trust its public key, so keep it: a new key means updating every template.

proxy.description: A socks5:// URL agent connections go through, e.g. "ssh -D" into the Quicksand host while developing elsewhere.

network.description: The network agent NICs are on (see docs/proxmox-setup.md).

bridge.description: The SDN VNet (with "Isolate Ports") agent NICs attach to.

subnet.description: Subnet agent NICs are addressed from.

serverIP.description: Quicksand's own address on the agent network. Agents only accept connections from it (enforced by the VM firewall).

macPrefix.description: First three bytes of agent NIC MACs.

nic.description: VM network device used for the agent.

model.description: NIC model (e1000 needs no guest drivers).

expiry.description: Destroys VMs a time limit after they are deployed unless their owners extend them. Without a time limit, VMs never expire. VMs deployed before expiry was configured get a full time limit from when the server starts.

timeLimit.description: How long after deploying a VM is destroyed. Unset or empty: VMs don't expire.

maxExtends.description: How many times an owner may extend a VM. Unset: no limit; 0: never. Administrators can always extend.

suspend.description: Hibernates running VMs (saving their memory to disk and stopping them) once nobody has used them for a while, freeing memory and CPU on Proxmox until their owners resume them. A VM is in use while it has a console, shell, port forward, file transfer or other agent session open. Doesn't affect expiry. Without an idle time, VMs are never suspended.

idleTime.description: How long a running VM may go unused before it's hibernated. Unset or empty: VMs aren't suspended.

quota.description: Limits how many VMs exist at once across all templates. Unset limits are unlimited.

links.description: Enables link networks: private networks users join their VMs into. Each is a VLAN on bridge; each linked VM gets an extra NIC there, unfiltered, with an address from subnet that its agent sets (or the user, without an agent). See docs/proxmox-setup.md.

bridge.description: A VLAN-aware bridge with no uplink, such as the internal bridge the agent VNet is on (vmbr9), so link networks reach nothing else.

vlans.description: VLAN tags link networks are given, one each. Must not include the agent network's tag (Quicksand refuses to start if it does).

subnet.description: Subnet linked VMs are addressed from. A VM keeps its address while it exists, through merges. Must not overlap the agent subnet.

macPrefix.description: First three bytes of link NIC MACs; must differ from the agent network's.

nic.description: VM network device used for links.

model.description: NIC model (e1000 needs no guest drivers).

audit.description: The audit log of what users do (sign-ins, deploys, shells, file transfers, administration), shown on the Admin page.

retention.description: How long entries are kept; older ones are deleted hourly. "0d" keeps them forever.

oidc.description: Enables single sign-on with an OpenID Connect provider such as Keycloak, alongside password sign-in (or instead of it, with disablePasswords). Users are created on their first sign-in. See docs/authentication.md.

issuer.description: The provider's issuer URL. For Keycloak, the realm's URL.

clientId.description: The client ID registered with the provider.

clientSecret.description: The client's secret (Keycloak: the client's Credentials tab, with client authentication on).

redirectURL.description: The callback URL registered with the provider: Quicksand's address followed by /api/auth/oidc/callback.

usernameClaim.description: ID token claim users are named by. Usernames are 1-64 letters, digits, '.', '_', '-', '@' or '+'.

groupsClaim.description: ID token claim listing the user's groups. Keycloak needs a Group Membership mapper to send it.

adminGroups.description: Members of any of these groups are administrators, and other single sign-on users are not, checked at each sign-in. A leading '/' (Keycloak's full group paths) is ignored. Without it, administrators are chosen on the Admin page.

allowedGroups.description: If set, only members of these groups (or of adminGroups) can sign in.

linkLocalUsers.description: Let a user's first single sign-on take over the existing password user of the same name, instead of refusing it. Enable only if the provider controls usernames.

disablePasswords.description: Turn off password sign-in, leaving single sign-on as the only way in.

duration.description: A duration: Go's syntax ("90m", "36h", "1h30m") plus days ("7d", "1d12h").

user.description: The most VMs one user may have. Unset: no limit.

global.description: The most VMs there may be across all users. Unset: no limit.

id.description: Identifies the template in the API and database; it must not change.

node.description: The Proxmox node the template is on.

name.description: What users see; defaults to the ID.

os.description: A hint for the icon shown, and how guest features behave.

fullClone.description: Copy the template's disks instead of linking to them.

cores.description: Default CPUs; 0 uses the template's own.

memoryMiB.description: Default memory in MiB; 0 uses the template's own.

maxCores.description: Most CPUs offered in the deploy dialog.

maxMemoryMiB.description: Most memory offered in the deploy dialog, in MiB.

agent.description: The template has the Quicksand agent installed; clones get a NIC on the agent network.

filesDir.description: The guest's default path: where file browsing, shells and relative paths (e.g. qs upload/download) start. Empty: the root of the filesystem (/, or the system drive on Windows).

quota.description: Limits how many VMs of this template exist at once. Unset limits are unlimited.

icon.description: File name of an image in the icons folder next to this configuration file (e.g. /etc/quicksand/icons), shown for the template instead of its OS's icon: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG, at most 512 KiB. Read when Quicksand starts.

serial.description: Enables shells over this serial port (added as a socket when deploying if the template lacks it). The guest must run a login prompt on it.

launch.description: Has the agent keep an app running in the guest's desktop session, as the signed-in user (Linux and Windows guests). Needs agent. Several templates can share one Proxmox template (vmid), each launching a different app. See docs/agent.md.

command.description: The program and its arguments. No shell is involved.

openURL.description: Lets the template open links: deploying it with a URL (e.g. from "Open in Quicksand") starts the app with this command instead, with {url} replaced by the URL as part of one argument. Only http and https URLs are accepted.

restart.description: Start the app again whenever it exits. Otherwise it's started once each time someone signs in to the guest.

id.description: Identifies the network in the API; it must not change.

bridge.description: A Proxmox bridge or SDN VNet. Null (or omitted) means isolated: the guest gets no network interface at all.

vlan.description: Tags the guest's interface on the bridge.

label.description: What users see; defaults to the ID.

default.description: Used when none is chosen; the first network if none is marked.
